title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A comment no longer hides your usages
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.33 fixes a bug our own previous fix introduced: a `"""` written inside a comment made Find Usages treat the rest of the file as text, so a symbol read "0 usages" and Rename left the old name behind. Large JDK classes such as `Arrays` and `Pattern` are navigable again, and the language server no longer misses a file whose folder name contains a comma or an ampersand.

highlights.title: Usages survive a comment
highlights.description: A `"""` written in a comment used to turn the rest of the file into text: no usages, and Rename left the old name behind in code that then failed to compile.

highlights.title: Big JDK classes navigable
highlights.description: `Arrays`, `Collections`, `Character`, `Pattern` and `BigDecimal` sit above the old 200 KB limit and were never indexed.

highlights.title: Right result on the right test
highlights.description: A test with no result of its own inherited the `@DisplayName`, the state and the failure trace of the test above it.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A `"""` inside a `//` or `/* */` comment no longer opens a raw string that swallows the rest of the file for Find Usages, Go to References and Rename.
The `@DisplayName` walk stops at a blank line and at a one line declaration, so a test no longer inherits its neighbour's result.
JDK sources larger than 200 KB are indexed, which covers `Arrays`, `Collections`, `Pattern` and `BigDecimal`.
The language server compares files by path, so a folder named with a comma or an ampersand no longer breaks deletion tracking and unsaved buffer reads.
The MCP `get_file_symbols` tool is bounded like the others.
